summary: Subaru's cheapest EV is the electric twin of the Toyota C-HR+ and is sold in Australia as a single, fully-loaded dual-motor AWD grade (now badged MY27) at $59,990 before on-roads, with 252kW, a 74.7kWh gross (71kWh usable) battery and 522km of WLTP range. Australian road tests split on it: CarExpert rates it Very Good for its sporty character, comfortable cabin and undercutting of direct rivals, while Chasing Cars scores it 6/10, calling it an innovative concept hobbled by an average platform with persistent understeer and a cramped rear seat. Both tests used more energy than claimed (17.8 and 18.3kWh/100km against 16.0), so expect nearer 400-460km of real range.
pros: Only one grade and it is the loaded one: 20-inch alloys, 14-inch touchscreen, 10-speaker Harman Kardon audio, heated front and rear outboard seats, power tailgate, digital rear-view mirror and 1500W V2L are all standard; a roof pack is a $1,200 option

252kW dual-motor Symmetrical AWD for a 5.0-second 0-100km/h, with 211mm of ground clearance - CarExpert and Chasing Cars both found it quick and predictable on dirt, which no front-drive-only rival at the price offers
22kW three-phase AC charging alongside 150kW DC (10-80% in about 30 minutes claimed), where most small electric SUVs cap AC at 7-11kW
Uses the same 74.7kWh gross battery and 252kW output as the larger Solterra AWD in a lighter, quicker body for $2,000 less list price
Five-year unlimited-km warranty with eight years/160,000km on the battery, and five years of capped-price servicing totalling $984
cons: Subaru Australia publishes no towing rating for it and offers no genuine towbar (the Trailseeker gets a 1,500kg-braked accessory); European cars and CarExpert's review quote 1,500kg braked, so confirm with Subaru before buying to tow

403 litres behind the rear seat (to the window line) and about 1,089 litres folded is small for the money, there is no spare wheel, and both Australian road tests call the fastback's rear seat cramped
$59,990 is top-of-segment for a small electric SUV - a Kia EV3 opens well over $10,000 below it - and CarExpert puts it at about $65,100 drive-away in Sydney
Real-world use ran 17.8-18.3kWh/100km in Australian tests against the 16.0 claim, and the 20-inch wheels are the only fitment, with no longer-range smaller-wheel configuration as offered overseas
Subaru cut Solterra prices by $2,000 and Trailseeker prices by $4,000 on the very day the Uncharted was priced, an uncomfortable precedent for early-buyer resale
